title: Idea → System (Risograph Printing, style-049)

scenes.title: Two-ink print run: idea to connected system
scenes.purpose: Show an idea (a halftone disc holding a bulb mark) printed as a two-ink riso sheet that becomes a connected network. The sheet is built separation by separation on cool blue-grey recycled stock.
visuals: Cool blue-grey recycled paper (#DDE3E2) with fixed fibre flecks and a soft vignette, all stationary
Coral ink separation: diagonal hatch band, halftone idea disc, idea block and offset node discs
Blue ink separation: ring, bulb mark, network links, nodes and headline, at a fixed +5/-4 px registration offset
Multiply overprint, so blue over coral prints darker
A fixed seeded grain mask with dropouts on each ink, plus static rough-edge displacement
A paper knockout box in the hatch band holding the caption

beats.development: Coral drum pass: a roller wipe prints the coral hatch band, halftone disc and idea block from left to right. 'IDEA' is set in coral and then overprinted in blue, settling into register.
The blue ring draws around the halftone disc, and the bulb mark and base strokes draw inside the idea.

The '→' word is set. Links draw outward from the idea; each node stamps first in coral, then in blue with an offset that settles into a stable registration. 'SYSTEM' completes the headline, and the paper knockout box opens in the hatch band.
The caption appears inside the completed knockout box. The finished two-ink sheet holds still for reading.
captions: AN IDEA BECOMES A CONNECTED SYSTEM — 2 INKS / BLUE + CORAL

findings: The headline is built additively at 0.30, 1.00 and 1.48 s, following the network build, which is the primary focus.
All motion ends by 2.0 s, which is well before the 2.7 s settle requirement.
Grain, paper and the registration offset stay stationary, with no per-frame re-randomisation.
justifiedHolds: 2.0–3.0 s: the completed sheet holds still so the headline and the 58-character caption can be read.

notes: Silent preview: no music, effects or voice.

No tech.preview_recipes were supplied, so this refresh demonstrates the primary implementation (limited ink separations, fixed grain, controlled registration offsets, animated layer reveals) together with the source-frame lessons: multiply overprint, stable grain with dropouts, a hatch motif with a paper knockout box, and an additive word build.

The background was changed from the prior warm cream to cool recycled stock, a tech/explainer choice listed in BACKGROUND_REVIEW. The two inks keep their roles: blue for type and lines, coral for pattern and fields.
The ink, grain and overprint are procedural SVG approximations, not a physical print.

Headline misregistration: the coral pass reuses the blue glyph outlines through SVG <use> clones placed at a fixed (+5,+8) px offset. The only readable headline text is the blue ink type (about 7:1 contrast on paper), and the coral layer is decorative ink, not a duplicate text block.
